body: Hmmm.... looks like I spoke too soon: `ExceptionHandlingTests.exceptionInAfterAllCallbackDoesNotHideFailureWhenTestInstancePerClassIsUsed()` now fails with my proposed _fix_.

In attempt to convey our discussion on Gitter, I think we discussed 3 different topics. All the case below are referring to test classes configured with `PER_CLASS` lifecycle semantics.

- a) Why Jupiter would not run instance methods annotated with `@BeforeAll` or `@AfterAll` when we have a failing constructor. The conclusion for this was that it is _impossible_ for these methods to run since no instance can be created.
- b) Why Jupiter would not run `static` methods annotated with `@BeforeAll` or `@AfterAll` when we have a failing constructor. Technically there is no restriction why these would not run, so it is a matter of design what the expected behavior here would be. 
  - On the one hand, having a `PER_CLASS` class failing on the constructor suggests a major problem that warrants aborting everything. Also why run `@BeforeAll` of `@AfterAll` when we have run none tests? 
  - On the other hand, this seems inconsistent with what we do for classes that are instantiated per method where a failing constructor does not affect the execution of methods annotated with `@BeforeAll` or `@AfterAll`.  So I personally consider this as unexpected behavior.
- c) Why Jupiter would run `AfterAllCallback` while not running everything else.
  - By the current title of this issue this point is the one handled by this issue. 

Also my understanding from the conversation on Gitter was that @beluha raised the issue because she also expected that `@BeforeAll` and `@AfterAll` methods should be running.

@beluha, Could you please clarify what you expected?

Thanks

> - a) Why Jupiter would not run instance methods annotated with `@BeforeAll` or `@AfterAll` when we have a failing constructor. The conclusion for this was that it is _impossible_ for these methods to run since no instance can be created.

That's correct: we cannot achieve the literally impossible. 😉

> - c) Why Jupiter would run `AfterAllCallback` while not running everything else.
>   - By the current title of this issue this point is the one handled by this issue. 

That's correct: as a general rule of thumb, JUnit Jupiter never runs AfterX methods or callbacks unless it ran (or attempted to run) BeforeX methods or callbacks.

The framework has been consistent in this regard, and whenever we notice anything to the contrary... we fix it (like in this issue).

> Also my understanding from the conversation on Gitter was that @beluha raised the issue because she also expected that `@BeforeAll` and `@AfterAll` callbacks should be running.

I'm not sure if you are referring to the callbacks (extensions) or user methods here.

In any case, I understood her desire differently.

So, yes, @beluha, could you please clarify what you expected?
